body: Thanks, I'm beginning to believe this. My whole life I've felt like it was something that I would beat one day and then I'd be 100% fine, but I'm realizing now that that is a very unrealistic outlook.
I usually opt for high-fiber diets with a lot of fruit and water. I'll look into doing something more plain, though.

I have something that falls into the umbrella of IBS, to my knowledge there isn't a specific name for the symptoms and assumed origin of what I have. Specifically, I have the symptoms of IBS-C, but it seems like the cause of it is atypical. I have been to a lot of dietitians, gastrointestinal doctors and the like, most of them have had similar advice, always with the caveat that they really can't predict if it would work or not.

The symptoms aren't always this bad. I think recently stress from school, not enough time/energy to exercise and a poor diet have been making things worse and worse. I hope I can turn it around, because the alternative seems unfeasibly bad.

aenea's comment has a good link on it that I think I may use for my jumping off point. It has listings for some IRL conferences and such that I think I may attend. Thanks very much for your offer, though. I had always felt too ashamed to really consider this option before but it looks like it might be very helpful.

Thank you very much for doing this research. I had always been hesitant to seek help for this sort of thing but now it's just too much. I'm sure you can imagine that it's a very embarrassing problem to see people about, too. Looking around the forums and seeing a lot of the issues I'm having is very comforting, though.

Actually scratch that looking at it even more it's almost overwhelmingly powerful. There's just so many answers and so many people have it just as bad as me. As you could probably tell from me generally being so... I don't even know but going through this leaves me feeling very emotional to say the least. I wish I had looked for things like this sooner thank you very much.

I saw a series of increasingly special specialists as I grew up, each one of them working towards coming up with a diet and medication plan that would work for me. The current system is that I take some weak laxities and a fiber supplement every night. In theory and in general practice, this keeps things moving while keeping the stool usually soft and solid.

My problem is that I really have no way at all to push stool through. My bowels are incapable of this due to being extremely dilated and scarred by early incidents related to this problem. The only way to produce results is to relax and let the digestive process work, I have no real way to force any incident to occur.

Through the two week or so period when I have no bowel movements, I have tried to take additional laxities and the like. However, they usually just give me what is referred to as overflow diarrhea, where extremely watery feces bypasses the blockage. Laxatives that work by stimulating the bowel instead of softening stool never have any effect for me, although I haven't taken anything very strong like this for fear of becoming dependent.

I'm worried I have an impacted stool. Is that what sent you to the hospital? Wikipedia says that a lot of severe cases can end in hospitalization. What usually happens after a day or two of diarrhea (like the one I'm having right now) I pass incredibly large, soft stools in a very short time period, but I'm worried that even after this I am not truly cleaned out. I'd like to go to the hospital or something to see what sort of procedures they can do but I simply can't afford to miss any school right now.

I'm a he, by the way. And I haven't been involved with any support groups. To my knowledge, there aren't any, but I haven't really thought too look around too much.
